examples.ko: 이번 달 지출액이 지난달보다 많이 늘었어요.
examples.en: This month's spending went up a lot compared to last month.

examples.ko: 가계부를 쓰면 한 달 지출액을 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep a household ledger, you can see a month's spending at a glance.

examples.ko: 지출액 중에서 식비가 가장 큰 부분을 차지해요.
examples.en: Of all my expenses, food takes up the biggest part.
I'm cutting back on eating out to reduce my spending.
My salary stays the same, but only my expenses keep growing.

examples.ko: 지출액과 수입액을 비교해서 표로 만들어 봤어요.
examples.en: I compared my expenses and income and made a table.

explain: '수입액'과 짝으로 써서 번 돈과 쓴 돈을 비교할 때 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '쓴 돈', '나간 돈'이라고도 말해요. '늘다/줄다', '많다/적다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It pairs with '수입액' (income) when comparing money earned and money spent. In everyday talk people also say '쓴 돈' or '나간 돈'. It goes well with '늘다/줄다' and '많다/적다'.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 마당에 지푸라기가 여기저기 널려 있어요.
examples.en: Straw is scattered all over the yard at my grandmother's house.
You have straw stuck on your clothes. Didn't you notice?
In the old days, people made shoes out of straw and wore them.

examples.ko: 아기 돼지 이야기에서 첫째는 지푸라기로 집을 지어요.
examples.en: In the story of the three little pigs, the first one builds a house of straw.
I wove straw together and made a small basket.

examples.ko: 바닥에 지푸라기 하나 안 남기고 깨끗이 치웠어요.
examples.en: I cleaned up so well that not a single piece of straw was left on the floor.

explain: 짚 한 가닥이나 부스러기처럼 작고 가벼운 것을 가리켜서 '지푸라기 하나'처럼 하나씩 셀 때도 많아요. 비유로 쓰일 때는 힘없고 약한 것을 말하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 너무 급해서 물에 빠지면 지푸라기라도 잡는다고 아무 방법이나 써 봤어요.
phrases.en: I was so desperate that I tried any method at all, like a drowning person clutching at straws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 급하고 절박하면 도움이 안 될 것 같은 것에도 매달린다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when people are desperate, they cling even to things that probably won't help.

explain_en: It often points to small, light bits of straw, so people count it like '지푸라기 하나' (a single piece of straw). In figurative use it carries a feeling of something weak and fragile.

examples.en: On rainy days, I shop in the underground mall.
The underground mall is cool in summer and warm in winter.
I bought cheap, pretty clothes at the underground mall.
I don't know where the entrance to the underground mall is.
I walked once around the underground mall with my friend.

examples.ko: 이 지하상가는 길이 복잡해서 자주 길을 잃어요.
examples.en: The paths in this underground mall are complicated, so I often get lost.

explain: 지하철역 근처 지하 통로를 따라 가게가 쭉 이어진 곳을 말해요. 백화점이나 마트의 '지하 매장'과는 달리 여러 작은 가게가 모여 있는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a place where many shops line an underground passage, often near a subway station. Unlike the basement floor of a department store or mart, it feels like a cluster of many small shops.

examples.en: Korea is a country without many underground resources.
Oil and coal are typical underground resources.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 지하자원을 수출해서 돈을 벌어요.
examples.en: That country earns money by exporting its underground resources.
If you dig up underground resources excessively, the environment gets damaged.
I envy countries rich in underground resources.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 지하자원 개발에 관한 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about developing underground resources on the news.

explain: 석유, 석탄, 철, 금처럼 땅속에서 나오는 자원을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이에요. '풍부하다/부족하다', '개발하다/캐다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is a collective term for resources from underground such as oil, coal, iron and gold. It often appears with '풍부하다/부족하다' (abundant/lacking) and '개발하다/캐다' (develop/dig).

examples.en: When the conductor raised the baton, the performance began.
The teacher pointed at the blackboard with a pointer stick.
The child waves chopsticks around like a baton.

examples.ko: 이 지휘봉은 가볍고 손에 잘 잡혀요.
examples.en: This baton is light and fits well in the hand.
I received a new baton as a gift.

examples.ko: 지휘봉을 잡은 지 벌써 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has already been ten years since I took up the baton.

explain: 음악 지휘자가 쓰는 막대기를 말하지만, 설명할 때 가리키는 막대기를 부를 때도 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '지휘봉을 잡다'가 감독이나 사령탑을 맡았다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: A new manager took over the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 막대기가 아니라 팀이나 조직을 이끄는 책임을 맡는다는 뜻으로, 주로 스포츠 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean an actual stick but taking charge of leading a team or organization, mostly used in sports news.

explain_en: It means the stick a conductor uses, but it is sometimes used for a pointer stick used when explaining. In the news, '지휘봉을 잡다' often means someone became a coach or head of a team.

examples.en: Medicine should be stored away from direct sunlight.

examples.ko: 직사광선 아래에 오래 있으면 피부가 상해요.
examples.en: If you stay under direct sunlight for long, your skin gets damaged.

examples.ko: 화분을 직사광선이 드는 창가에 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't put the plant pot on a windowsill that gets direct sunlight.

examples.ko: 직사광선에 차를 세워 두었더니 안이 너무 뜨거워요.
examples.en: I left the car in direct sunlight, and it's very hot inside.

examples.ko: 이 책은 직사광선 때문에 색이 바랬어요.
examples.en: The color of this book faded because of direct sunlight.
I hung curtains that block direct sunlight.

explain: '햇빛' 중에서도 중간에 가려지지 않고 곧바로 내리쬐는 빛을 말해서, 보관 방법 안내문에 '직사광선을 피하세요'로 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '햇빛'이라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: It means sunlight that shines straight down with nothing blocking it, and it often appears in storage instructions as '직사광선을 피하세요'. In daily talk, simply saying '햇빛' is also fine.

examples.en: The straight-line distance from my house to school is about one kilometer.
It's close in a straight line, but far by road.
What is the straight-line distance between the two cities?
I measured the straight-line distance on the map.
To go in a straight line, you have to cross the mountain.

examples.ko: 서울과 부산의 직선거리는 삼백 킬로미터가 넘어요.
examples.en: The straight-line distance between Seoul and Busan is over three hundred kilometers.

explain: 길을 따라 실제로 가는 거리가 아니라 두 곳을 곧게 이은 거리예요. 그래서 '직선거리로는 가깝다'처럼 실제 이동 거리와 비교할 때 많이 말해요. 실제 이동 거리는 보통 '도로 거리'나 '걸리는 시간'으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the distance of a straight line between two points, not the distance you actually travel along roads. That is why people say things like '직선거리로는 가깝다' to compare it with the real trip. The actual travel distance is usually described as '도로 거리' or by travel time.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 유럽에서 직수입한 가구를 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop sells furniture directly imported from Europe.

examples.ko: 직수입 제품은 값이 조금 더 싸요.
examples.en: Directly imported products are a bit cheaper.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 직수입이라서 다른 데서는 못 사요.
examples.en: This snack is a direct import, so you can't buy it elsewhere.

examples.ko: 직수입 화장품만 모아 놓은 가게를 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a store that gathers only directly imported cosmetics.

examples.ko: 이 커피는 농장에서 바로 직수입해 온 거예요.
examples.en: This coffee was imported directly from the farm.

examples.ko: 직수입으로 들여오면 중간 유통 비용이 줄어요.
examples.en: If you bring it in by direct import, the middleman costs go down.

explain: 수입 업체를 거치지 않고 가게나 회사가 외국에서 직접 들여오는 것을 말해요. 광고나 가게 설명에서 '직수입'이라고 많이 붙여요. '수입'만 쓰는 것보다 중간 단계가 없다는 느낌이 더해져요.
explain_en: It means a shop or company brings goods in from abroad itself without going through an importer. You often see '직수입' attached in ads and shop descriptions. Compared with plain '수입', it adds the feeling that there is no middle step.

examples.en: I was introduced to a job at an employment agency.
I went to an employment agency and got a consultation.
This employment agency doesn't charge a fee.
I found a part-time job through the local employment agency.
The employment agency staff explained things kindly.
I submitted my resume to the employment agency and am waiting for a call.

explain: 일자리를 찾는 사람과 사람을 구하는 곳을 이어 주는 곳이에요. 요즘은 '취업 사이트'나 '앱'으로 구하는 사람도 많아서 일상 대화에서는 '일자리 구하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a place that connects people looking for work with employers who need workers. These days many people use job sites or apps, so in everyday talk they more often say '일자리 구하다' (look for a job).

examples.en: Sleet has been falling since morning, so the road is muddy.

examples.ko: 눈도 아니고 비도 아닌 진눈깨비가 오네요.
examples.en: It's sleet, neither snow nor rain.
My shoes got completely wet because of the sleet.
Driving is hard on days when it sleets.
They say the sleet will turn into snow in the afternoon.
I waited for the bus in the sleet.

explain: 비와 눈이 섞여서 내리는 것을 말해요. '진눈깨비가 오다/내리다'처럼 쓰고, 땅이 질척해지는 날씨 느낌이 있어서 '길이 질척하다'와 자주 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is precipitation where rain and snow fall mixed together. You say '진눈깨비가 오다/내리다', and it carries the feeling of slushy weather, so it often goes with '길이 질척하다' (the road is muddy).

en: medical examination and treatment fee; medical service fee

examples.ko: 병원에서 건강 보험이 적용되면 진료비가 훨씬 줄어요.
examples.en: If health insurance applies at the hospital, the medical fee goes down a lot.

examples.ko: 진료비는 접수할 때 먼저 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay the medical fee first when you register.

examples.ko: 감기로 병원에 갔는데 진료비가 생각보다 적게 나왔어요.
examples.en: I went to the hospital for a cold, and the fee was lower than I expected.
Please keep your medical fee receipt safe.

examples.ko: 아이 진료비는 나라에서 일부 지원해 줘요.
examples.en: The government supports part of children's medical fees.
Can I pay the medical fee by card?

explain: 의사에게 진찰을 받고 치료받는 데 드는 돈을 말해요. 약값은 '약값'이나 '약제비'로 따로 말하는 경우가 많고, 입원하면 '입원비'가 더해져요.
explain_en: It is the money for seeing a doctor and receiving treatment. Medicine costs are often mentioned separately as '약값' or '약제비', and a hospital stay adds '입원비'.

examples.en: I can feel sincerity in that person's words.
The truthfulness of this article is doubtful.
A sincere apology is the most important.

examples.ko: 광고에 진실성이 없으면 사람들이 믿지 않아요.
examples.en: If an advertisement has no truthfulness, people don't believe it.
I spoke frankly to show my sincerity.
His sincerity came through in his letter.

explain: 말이나 행동이 거짓 없이 진짜라는 성질을 말해서 '진실성이 있다/없다/느껴지다'로 자주 써요. 사람에게도 쓰지만 기사, 광고, 사과처럼 내용이나 태도에 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It names the quality of words or actions being genuine and without lies, used as '진실성이 있다/없다/느껴지다'. It can describe a person, but is used more for content or attitude, such as articles, ads and apologies.

examples.ko: 진열대 가격표를 보고 손님들 눈이 휘둥그레졌어요.
examples.en: The customers' eyes grew wide when they saw the price tags on the display stand.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 과자가 진열대 맨 앞에 있어요.
examples.en: The newly released snack is at the very front of the display stand.
I filled the display stand with goods neatly.
A child is running around between the shelves in the mart.

examples.ko: 인기 상품은 금방 팔려서 진열대가 비었어요.
examples.en: The popular items sold out quickly, so the display stand is empty.

examples.ko: 이 진열대는 높아서 손이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: This display stand is so high that I can't reach it.

explain: 가게에서 물건을 올려 두고 보여 주는 선반이에요. 유리로 닫힌 '진열장'과 달리 열려 있어서 손님이 바로 집을 수 있는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a shelf in a shop where goods are placed to show them. Unlike a glass-enclosed '진열장', it is open, giving the feeling that customers can pick things up directly.

examples.en: The display case is full of pretty dishes.

examples.ko: 가게 진열장에 있는 가방이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the bag in the shop's display case.
My grandmother put family photos in the display cabinet.
I wiped the glass of the display case clean.

examples.ko: 박물관 진열장 속의 옛날 동전을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I looked at the old coins inside the museum's display case.
I asked the clerk to take it out of the display case.

explain: 유리문이나 유리 벽이 있어서 안에 든 물건을 보여 주는 장이에요. 열린 선반인 '진열대'와 달리 손님이 마음대로 집기 어려워서 비싼 물건이나 귀한 물건을 넣어요.
explain_en: It is a cabinet with glass doors or walls that shows what is inside. Unlike the open shelf '진열대', customers can't freely pick things up, so expensive or precious items are put in it.

examples.en: Yesterday I felt lonely and just cried all day.
It rained, so I stayed home all day.
I walked all day, so my legs hurt a lot.
I'm worried because my child plays games all day.
I waited all day, but there's no word.
Yesterday I did nothing but clean all day.

explain: '하루 종일', '종일'과 같은 뜻으로, 아침부터 저녁까지 쭉 이어진 것을 나타내요. 뒤에 '울기만 하다', '집에만 있다'처럼 한 가지 일이 계속된다는 말이 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is the same as '하루 종일' or '종일', meaning something continued from morning to evening. It is often followed by phrases like '울기만 하다' or '집에만 있다', showing that one thing kept going.

examples.ko: 그 얘기를 진즉 했어야 했는데 미안해요.
examples.en: I should have told you that earlier. I'm sorry.
If I had known earlier, I would have gone with you.
Why didn't you tell me earlier?
I finished the homework a while ago.

examples.ko: 진즉 병원에 갔더라면 덜 아팠을 거예요.
examples.en: If I had gone to the hospital earlier, it would have hurt less.
That person left long ago.

explain: '진작'과 같은 뜻으로, 이미 한참 전에 했어야 하거나 이미 했다는 말이에요. '진즉 알았으면', '진즉 말하지'처럼 후회나 아쉬움을 나타낼 때 특히 많이 써요.
explain_en: It has the same meaning as '진작', pointing to something that should have happened long ago or already did. It is used especially for regret or disappointment, as in '진즉 알았으면' or '진즉 말하지'.

examples.en: This place's kimchi stew has the real deal taste.
A genuine leather bag is expensive.
That singer's singing skill is the real thing.
I bought genuine sesame oil at the market.
It's not easy to tell the real thing from a fake.
He's a true expert technician with long experience.

explain: '진짜'보다 더 구어체이고, 겉모양만 그럴듯한 것이 아니라 알맹이까지 제대로인 것을 칭찬하는 느낌이에요. 음식, 물건, 실력 있는 사람에게 두루 쓰고 반대는 '가짜'예요.
explain_en: It is more colloquial than '진짜' and praises something that is genuine all the way through, not just in appearance. It is used for food, goods and skilled people, and its opposite is '가짜' (fake).

examples.en: I learned Darwin's theory of evolution at school.
I'm reading a book about the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 진화론은 생물이 환경에 맞게 변해 왔다고 설명해요.
examples.en: The theory of evolution explains that living things have changed to fit their environment.
There was a long debate over the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에서는 진화론을 쉽게 소개해 줘요.
examples.en: This museum introduces the theory of evolution in an easy way.

examples.ko: 진화론이 나오기 전에는 사람들이 다르게 생각했어요.
examples.en: Before the theory of evolution appeared, people thought differently.

explain: '진화'는 실제로 일어나는 변화를 말하고, '진화론'은 그 변화를 다룬 이론을 말해요. 그래서 '진화가 일어나다'처럼 쓰지만, 이론은 '진화론이 나오다', '진화론을 배우다'처럼 써요. 보통 '창조론'과 짝으로 나오고, '다윈의 진화론'처럼 사람 이름과 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '진화' is the change that actually happens, while '진화론' is the theory about that change. So you say '진화가 일어나다' for the change itself, but '진화론이 나오다' or '진화론을 배우다' for the theory. It often appears paired with '창조론' (creationism), and commonly with a person's name, as in '다윈의 진화론'.

examples.en: I pointed toward the road with my index finger.
My index finger got caught in the door, and it hurts.
I picked up the bean with my index finger and thumb.

examples.ko: 아이가 집게손가락을 입술에 대고 조용히 하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child put an index finger to the lips and told us to be quiet.
I put a ring on my index finger.
I got a small cut on my index finger from a knife.

explain: 엄지 옆 손가락이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '검지'라고 짧게 말하는 경우가 많고, '둘째손가락'이라고도 해요. 물건을 집거나 가리킬 때 쓰는 손가락이라서 '집게'라는 말이 붙었어요.
explain_en: It is the finger next to the thumb. In everyday talk people often say the shorter '검지', and '둘째손가락' also exists. It is the finger used to pick things up or point, which is where '집게' comes from.

examples.en: When you live communally in a dormitory, rules are important.
Ants are insects that live in groups.
It's my first time living in a group, so I'm very nervous.
Children learn group life at kindergarten.
In group life, it is important to consider one another.
Group life is hard, so I want to spend time alone.

explain: 여러 사람이나 동물이 한 곳에서 함께 지내는 생활이에요. 사람에게는 기숙사, 군대, 유치원 같은 곳을 떠올리게 하고, '집단생활을 하다'로 많이 써요. 혼자 지내는 '독립생활'이나 '혼자 사는 생활'과 대비돼요.
explain_en: It is life where many people or animals stay together in one place. For people it brings to mind dormitories, the military or kindergarten, and it is commonly used as '집단생활을 하다'. It contrasts with living alone.

examples.en: It's an old house, so we need to do repairs.
This weekend I did home repairs with my father.
The home repair cost more than I thought.
It was noisy all day because of the home repair work.

examples.ko: 집수리를 맡길 만한 업체를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company I can trust with home repairs.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 급하게 집수리 기사님을 불렀어요.
examples.en: The roof leaked, so I urgently called a home repair technician.

explain: 고장 난 곳을 고치는 작은 일부터 집 안을 새로 꾸미는 큰 공사까지 넓게 말할 때 써요. '집수리를 하다/맡기다'로 쓰고, 큰 공사는 '리모델링'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It covers everything from small fixes of broken spots to larger work on a home. Use it as '집수리를 하다/맡기다'. For big jobs people also say '리모델링' (remodeling).

examples.ko: 힘들다고 하던 일을 집어치우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't quit what you were doing just because it's hard.
I want to quit my company and open a shop.
It's annoying, so drop that talk now.

examples.ko: 공부를 집어치우고 놀러 갈까 하는 생각도 들어요.
examples.en: I even think about dropping studying and going out to play.
I already gave up on that job.
Skip the excuses and tell me the truth.

explain: '그만두다'와 비슷하지만 화가 나거나 속상해서 거칠게 던져 버리는 느낌이 강해요. 윗사람에게 '집어치우세요'라고 하면 무례하니 친한 사이에서 쓰고, 정중하게 말할 때는 '그만두다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '그만두다' but carries a strong feeling of angrily throwing something away. Saying '집어치우세요' to someone older is rude, so use it with close people, and use '그만두다' to be polite.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방에 어깨가 짓눌리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My shoulders feel pressed down by the heavy bag.
I was weighed down by responsibility and couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 상자 아래에 있던 빵이 짓눌려서 납작해졌어요.
examples.en: The bread under the box got squashed and flattened.

examples.ko: 불안감에 짓눌릴 때는 잠깐 쉬어 보세요.
examples.en: When you feel crushed by anxiety, try taking a short rest.
A thick blanket pressed on me, and it was hard to breathe.
He was crushed by poverty and gave up his dream.

explain: 무거운 것에 눌린다는 물리적인 쓰임도 있지만, '책임감, 불안, 가난에 짓눌리다'처럼 마음이 무거워지는 말로 자주 써요. 단순히 '눌리다'보다 힘에 못 이겨 꼼짝 못 하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It can mean being physically pressed by something heavy, but it is often used for a heavy mind, as in '책임감, 불안, 가난에 짓눌리다'. Compared with plain '눌리다', it has a stronger feeling of being unable to move under the force.

examples.ko: 다음 달 징검다리 연휴에는 하루만 쉬면 닷새를 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: During next month's bridge holiday, if I take just one day off, I get five days of rest.

examples.ko: 징검다리 연휴에 여행 가려고 비행기 표를 미리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought plane tickets in advance to travel over the bridge holiday.

examples.ko: 시냇물에 놓인 징검다리를 건너서 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: I crossed the stepping stones in the stream to get to school.
The children carefully hop across the stepping stones.

examples.ko: 이번 경험이 다음 도전의 징검다리가 될 거예요.
examples.en: This experience will be a stepping stone for your next challenge.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 징검다리가 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the stepping stones were under water.

explain: 개울에 돌을 띄엄띄엄 놓아 건너게 한 길을 말하고, 그래서 '다음 단계로 가게 해 주는 것'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 달력에서는 휴일 사이에 평일 하루가 끼인 연휴를 '징검다리 연휴'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이번 징검다리 연휴에는 하루 휴가를 내고 고향에 가요.
phrases.en: For this bridge holiday, I'm taking one day of leave and going to my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 날 사이에 평일이 하루나 이틀 끼어서 군데군데 쉬는 연휴를 말해요. 돌을 띄엄띄엄 밟고 건너는 모습에서 나왔어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A holiday period where one or two workdays sit between days off, so the rest comes in separated chunks. The image is of stepping across stones set at intervals.

explain_en: It names a path of stones laid at intervals so you can cross a stream, and so it is often used figuratively for something that takes you to the next step. On the calendar, a holiday stretch with a single workday between days off is called a '징검다리 연휴'.

examples.en: The child keeps whining for me to buy it.
Don't whine, try saying it in words.
It's tiring because of my friend who whines about being tired.
My younger sibling has been whining since morning, so it's noisy.
You shouldn't whine even after you become an adult.

examples.ko: 징징거릴 시간에 하나라도 더 해 봐요.
examples.en: Instead of whining, try doing one more thing.

explain: '징징대다'와 같은 뜻으로, 우는소리를 내며 보채거나 불평하는 모습을 말해요. 아이에게 많이 쓰지만 어른이 힘들다고 계속 불평할 때도 쓰는데, 그때는 조금 핀잔하는 말투예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '징징대다', describing fussing or complaining in a crying tone. It is used a lot for children, but also for adults who keep complaining about hardship, in which case it sounds a bit scolding.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있었더니 다리가 짜릿짜릿 저려요.
examples.en: I sat for a long time, and my leg is tingling numb.
When I ride an amusement ride, my whole body tingles with thrill.
My fingertips tingled as if electricity had passed through.

examples.ko: 응원하는 팀이 이기는 순간 가슴이 짜릿짜릿했어요.
examples.en: My heart thrilled the moment the team I cheered for won.
I put my hand in cold water, and it stings with a tingle.

examples.ko: 발이 짜릿짜릿 저리니까 잠깐 걷고 올게요.
examples.en: My foot is tingling numb, so I'll walk around for a bit.

explain: 몸에 약한 전기가 흐르는 듯한 느낌을 말하는데, 저린 느낌과 짜릿한 기분 두 가지에 모두 써요. 보통 '짜릿짜릿하다'로 쓰고, 기분 좋은 쪽은 '짜릿하다'라고 짧게도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a feeling like a weak electric current running through the body, and it covers both numb tingling and a thrilling sensation. It is usually used as '짜릿짜릿하다', and for the pleasant sense people also say the shorter '짜릿하다'.

examples.ko: 이 발표는 짜임새가 탄탄해서 질문이 거의 나오지 않았어요.
examples.en: This presentation was so well structured that hardly any questions came up.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 줄거리의 짜임새가 느슨해서 몰입이 안 됐어요.
examples.en: That movie's plot was loosely put together, so I couldn't get absorbed.
Please explain the structure of this sentence.

examples.ko: 방 짜임이 좋아서 좁아도 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: The room's layout is good, so it looks wide even though it's small.

examples.ko: 글의 짜임새를 먼저 생각하고 나서 써요.
examples.en: I think about the structure of the writing first, and then write.
The way the class schedule is put together is too tight.

explain: 여러 부분이 모여 이루어진 모양이나 구성을 말하는데, '짜임새'라는 형태로 더 자주 들려요. '짜임새가 탄탄하다/느슨하다'처럼 얼마나 잘 맞물려 있는지를 평가할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to how several parts are put together, and it is often heard in the form '짜임새'. You use it to judge how well things fit together, as in '짜임새가 탄탄하다/느슨하다' (tight/loose structure).

examples.en: I was in a hurry and went out wearing mismatched socks.
I didn't know my shoes were mismatched.
I wore mismatched earrings on purpose.
The child wearing mismatched gloves was cute.

examples.ko: 아침에 옷을 짝짝이로 입고 와서 친구들이 웃었어요.
examples.en: I came dressed in mismatched clothes this morning, and my friends laughed.

examples.ko: 눈 크기가 짝짝이라서 사진 찍을 때 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My eyes are different sizes, so I worry about it when taking photos.

explain: 양말, 신발, 장갑처럼 짝이 맞아야 하는 두 개가 서로 다르게 된 것을 말해요. 눈이나 귀처럼 양쪽이 비대칭인 모습에도 쓰고, 보통 '짝짝이로 신다/하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means two things that should match, such as socks, shoes or gloves, are different from each other. It is also used for uneven pairs like eyes or ears, and usually appears as '짝짝이로 신다/하다'.

examples.ko: 이 멸치볶음은 짭조름해서 밥이랑 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This stir-fried anchovy is nicely salty, so it goes well with rice.
I keep thinking about the lightly salty french fries.
The soup turned out a little salty.
The sea breeze had a salty smell.

examples.ko: 짭조름한 과자를 먹었더니 물이 마시고 싶어요.
examples.en: I ate a salty snack, so now I want water.
After adding soy sauce, the taste became pleasantly salty.

explain: '짜다'가 소금이 너무 많아 부담스러운 느낌일 때가 많다면, 이 말은 입맛을 당기는 알맞게 짠 맛에 더 어울려요. 밥반찬, 과자, 바닷바람의 냄새에도 써요.
explain_en: While '짜다' often feels too salty, this word suits a pleasantly salty taste that makes you want more. It is used for side dishes, snacks and even the smell of the sea breeze.

examples.en: Every morning sparrows chirp outside my window.

examples.ko: 새들이 짹짹 노래하는 소리에 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up to the sound of birds chirping.

examples.ko: 아기 새들이 짹짹 하고 어미를 불러요.
examples.en: The baby birds call for their mother with chirps.
I can hear a chirping sound from the tree.
Swallows twitter under the eaves.

examples.ko: 창문을 여니 짹짹 소리가 더 크게 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the window, the chirping sounded louder.

explain: 참새처럼 작은 새가 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 보통 '짹짹 울다/지저귀다'로 쓰고, 소리를 가리킬 때는 '짹짹 소리'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the cry of small birds like sparrows. It usually appears as '짹짹 울다/지저귀다', and for the sound itself people say '짹짹 소리'.

en: with a clink; with a clank

examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and shattered with a crash.
I heard a clanging sound in the kitchen and ran over.
The window broke with a clatter.

examples.ko: 접시를 놓치는 순간 쨍그랑 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I dropped the plate, it made a crashing sound.
The baby was startled by the crash and cried.
The coin rolled across the floor with a clink.

explain: 유리나 그릇 같은 단단하고 얇은 것이 깨지거나 부딪칠 때 나는 높은 소리예요. 소리가 더 크고 무거우면 '와장창'처럼 다른 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the high sound of hard, thin things like glass or dishes breaking or hitting something. For a louder, heavier crash, people may use other words such as '와장창'.

examples.en: It's a summer afternoon with the sun blazing down.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 비치는 햇볕 때문에 눈이 부셔요.
examples.en: The glaring sunshine is dazzling my eyes.

examples.ko: 어제는 해가 쨍쨍 나서 빨래가 잘 말랐어요.
examples.en: Yesterday the sun was shining brightly, so the laundry dried well.

examples.ko: 해가 쨍쨍 뜬 날에는 모자를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: On days when the sun is blazing, I always wear a hat.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 더운 날 밖에서 일하면 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working outside on a blazing hot day is hard.

examples.ko: 햇볕이 쨍쨍 나자 아이들이 물놀이를 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the sun came out brightly, the children started playing in the water.

explain: 햇볕이 아주 밝고 강하게 비치는 모양이에요. '해가 쨍쨍 나다', '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다'처럼 날씨 이야기에서 주로 쓰고, 구름이 없는 맑은 날의 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes sunlight shining very bright and strong. It mostly appears in weather talk, as in '해가 쨍쨍 나다' or '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다', and gives the feeling of a clear, cloudless day.

examples.en: The watermelon split in half as soon as the knife touched it.
The firewood splits when it is hit by an axe.

examples.ko: 그 큰 회사는 두 개로 쪼개졌어요.
examples.en: That big company was split into two.

examples.ko: 얼음이 햇볕에 녹아서 여러 조각으로 쪼개져요.
examples.en: The ice melts in the sun and splits into several pieces.
I was worried the cup would split when it fell.
Opinions are divided in two, so it's hard to decide.

explain: '깨지다'가 여러 조각이 되는 느낌이라면, '쪼개지다'는 한 덩어리가 힘을 받아 두 쪽이나 몇 쪽으로 갈라지는 느낌이에요. 능동형은 '쪼개다'이고, 회사나 의견이 나뉘는 모습에도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: While '깨지다' feels like breaking into many pieces, '쪼개지다' feels like one lump being forced apart into two or a few parts. The active form is '쪼개다', and it is also used figuratively for companies or opinions dividing.
